case_title: GURJIT SINGH v. STATE OF PUNJAB
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.498-A, acquitted under s.304-B
high_court_outcome: Maintained conviction under s.498-A, convicted under s.306
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the husband of the deceased, was alleged to have subjected the deceased to harassment with a view to coercing her and her parents to meet an unlawful demand for money. The deceased died by consuming poison approximately two months after the last visit to her parents regarding the illegal demand. The prosecution claimed that the harassment was part of a dowry demand, and the accused was charged under Section 498-A of the IPC. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 498-A but acquitted him for the offence punishable under Section 304-B. The High Court upheld the conviction under Section 498-A but also convicted the accused under Section 306 of the IPC, relying on the presumption under Section 113-A of the Evidence Act. However, the Supreme Court set aside the conviction under Section 306, finding that the prosecution failed to establish a proximate nexus between the harassment and the suicide, and that the charge did not specifically state that the deceased was driven to commit suicide due to the harassment.
